title: zellerlab/flexprofiler pipeline parameters
description: Taxonomic classification and profiling of metagenomic and 16S data

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to comma-separated file containing information about the samples and libraries/runs.
input.help_text: You will need to create a design file with information about the samples and libraries/runs you want to running in your pipeline run. Use this parameter to specify its location. It has to be a comma-separated file with 6 columns, and a header row. See [usage docs](docs/usage.md).

databases.description: Path to comma-separated file containing information about databases and profiling parameters for each taxonomic profiler
databases.help_text:
You will need to create a design file with information about the samples in your experiment before running the pipeline. Use this parameter to specify its location. It has to be a comma-separated file with 4 columns, and a header row. See [usage docs](docs/usage.md).

Profilers will only be executed if a corresponding  database are supplied. 

We recommend storing this database sheet somewhere centrally and accessible by others members of your lab/institutions, as this file will likely be regularly reused.

save_untarred_databases.description: Specify to save decompressed user-supplied TAR archives of databases
save_untarred_databases.help_text: If input databases are supplied as gzipped TAR archives, in some cases you may want to move and re-use these for future runs. Specifying this parameter will save these to `--outdir results/` under a directory called `untar`.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

preprocessing_general_qc_options.title: Preprocessing general QC options
preprocessing_general_qc_options.description: Common options across both long and short read preprocessing QC steps

perform_repair_pe_order.description: Use bbmap repair to attempt at repairing broken paired end reads
perform_repair_pe_order.help_text: BBMAP repair reorders reads in paired-end fastq files so that they are correctly matched.\nPE reads may become unmatched in case of upstream processing with non-PE-aware tools.\nRefer to https://github.com/BioInfoTools/BBMap/blob/master/sh/repair.sh for more information.

skip_preprocessing_qc.description: Specify to skip sequencing quality control of raw sequencing reads
skip_preprocessing_qc.help_text: Skipping running of FastQC or Falco maybe useful in cases where you are already running with preprocessed data (e.g. you are also skipping short/long read qc steps) that you already know the quality of

preprocessing_qc_tool.help_text: Falco (the default) is a drop-in replacement for FastQC written in C++, faster and with much less memory, especially with long reads. FastQC can be used instead with `fastqc`.
preprocessing_qc_tool.description: Specify the tool used for quality control of raw sequencing reads

save_preprocessed_reads.description: Save reads from samples that went through the adapter clipping, pair-merging, and length filtering steps of the short reads
save_preprocessed_reads.help_text:
This saves the FASTQ output of fastp.

These reads will be a mixture of: adapter clipped, quality trimmed, pair-merged, and length filtered, depending on the parameters you set.

save_analysis_ready_fastqs.description: Save only the final reads from all read processing steps (that are sent to classification/profiling) in results directory.
save_analysis_ready_fastqs.help_text:
This flag will generate the directory `results/analysis_ready_reads` that contains the reads from the last preprocessing (QC, host removal, run merging etc.) step of the pipeline run. 

This can be useful if you wish to re-use the final cleaned-up and prepared reads - the data actually used for the actual classification/profiling steps of the pipeline - for other analyses or purposes (e.g., to reduce redundant preprocessing between different pipelines, e.g. [nf-core/mag](https://nf-co.re/mag)).

In most cases this will be preferred over similar parameters e.g. ` --save_preprocessed_reads`, unless you wish to explore in more detail the output of each specific preprocessing step independently.

Note if you do no preprocessing of any kind, nothing will be present in this directory.

preprocessing_short_read_qc_options.title: Preprocessing short-read QC options
preprocessing_short_read_qc_options.description: Options for adapter clipping, quality trimming, and pair-merging

perform_amplicon_primertrimming.description: Find and trim the primers of amplicon reads (library_strategy AMPLICON), with PIMENTO and cutadapt
perform_amplicon_primertrimming.help_text: For each AMPLICON run, the primers are searched with PIMENTO (`pimento std`) against its standard primer library, separately for the two mates of paired-end reads. Long reads (PacBio), sequenced from either end of the amplicon, are first oriented with vsearch against `--amplicon_orient_reference`, and then searched as single-end reads. The primers can also be given (`--amplicon_primer_fwd`, `--amplicon_primer_rev`), instead of found with PIMENTO. If primers are found, they are trimmed with cutadapt after the QC of the reads and before the handling of the read pairs (`--amplicon_pair_handling`). Short reads: all the primers found are searched at the start of both mates (also trimming pairs sequenced in the other orientation), then their reverse complements at the end of the reads (reads running past the end of the amplicon). Long reads: the forward primer at the start and the reverse complement of the reverse primer at the end, both required (the reads without both primers are discarded, as in the best practice for PacBio full-length 16S), in either orientation, with a length window of 1000-1600 bp (full-length 16S, changed with `ext.args` of `CUTADAPT_LINKED`). Runs without primers are not trimmed. The PIMENTO and cutadapt options can be changed with `ext.args` in a custom config (see the usage documentation).

amplicon_primer_fwd.description: Forward primer of the amplicon reads, 5'-3' (IUPAC codes allowed), instead of finding the primers with PIMENTO. Requires --amplicon_primer_rev
amplicon_primer_fwd.help_text: With `--amplicon_primer_fwd` and `--amplicon_primer_rev`, the primers of all the AMPLICON runs are these, and PIMENTO is not run. Short reads: both primers are searched at the start of the reads (and mates), and their reverse complements at the end. Long reads: the forward primer at the start and the reverse complement of the reverse primer at the end, both required (the reads without both primers are discarded), in either orientation (cutadapt `--revcomp`, the reads are written in the orientation of the forward primer). E.g. for PacBio full-length 16S: `--amplicon_primer_fwd AGRGTTYGATYMTGGCTCAG --amplicon_primer_rev RGYTACCTTGTTACGACTT`.

amplicon_primer_rev.description: Reverse primer of the amplicon reads, 5'-3' on the reverse strand (IUPAC codes allowed), instead of finding the primers with PIMENTO. Requires --amplicon_primer_fwd

amplicon_orient_reference.description: Reference sequences (FASTA) of the gene of the long-read amplicons, in its orientation, to orient the reads before finding their primers with PIMENTO. Required with long-read AMPLICON runs, unless the primers are given
amplicon_orient_reference.help_text: Long reads (PacBio) are sequenced from either end of the amplicon, so, without the primers given (`--amplicon_primer_fwd`, `--amplicon_primer_rev`), they are first oriented with `vsearch --orient` against these sequences, of the same gene as the reads (e.g. 16S), all in the orientation of the gene. A few diverse sequences are enough, as only the strand is found: e.g. a 16S of a few bacterial phyla and an archaeon, or a 16S database such as GTDB `ssu_all`. The reads that cannot be oriented (not of the gene of the reference) are dropped.

amplicon_pimento_primers_pacbio.description: FASTA files of primers added to the PIMENTO standard library for the PacBio AMPLICON runs, one region per file (named as the file)
amplicon_pimento_primers_pacbio.help_text: The PIMENTO standard library has not the full-length 16S primers of PacBio (also used for Kinnex 16S): 27F `AGRGTTYGATYMTGGCTCAG` and 1492R `RGYTACCTTGTTACGACTT` (PacBio PN 101-599-700), which are added by default (`assets/pimento_primers/V1-V9_PacBio.fasta`, see `assets/pimento_primers/README.md`). Without them, PIMENTO finds its 27F and 1492modR in these reads, and cutadapt, requiring the 22 bases of 1492modR, 3 more than the end of the reads, discards nearly all of them. Several files can be given with a glob pattern. In the FASTA headers, the names of the forward primers end with `F`, those of the reverse primers with `R`. Not used with `--amplicon_primer_fwd` and `--amplicon_primer_rev`.

amplicon_pair_handling.description: How the read pairs of paired-end amplicon reads are made into single sequences
amplicon_pair_handling.help_text: The amplicon profilers (IDTAXA) classify single sequences, so the read pairs of the AMPLICON runs are handled at the end of their preprocessing, after primer trimming and before run merging. `merged_plus_joined`: the pairs are merged with vsearch if they overlap, and the others joined with a padding of Ns (R1, Ns, reverse complement of R2), so that each pair is classified once, as one sequence. `merged_plus_unmerged`: the pairs are merged with fastp if they overlap, and the two mates of the others are kept as separate sequences, so that such a pair counts twice in the profile. `none`: the pairs are kept as they are, e.g. to save them as analysis-ready reads for another tool (`--save_analysis_ready_fastqs`); the amplicon profilers cannot be run then. The analysis-ready reads of the AMPLICON runs are those after pair handling. The vsearch and fastp options can be changed with `ext.args` of `VSEARCH_MERGEJOIN` and `FASTP_AMPLICON_MERGE` in a custom config.

perform_shortread_qc.description: Turns on short read quality control steps (adapter clipping, quality trimming, pair merging etc.)
perform_shortread_qc.help_text:
Turns on short read quality control steps (adapter clipping, quality trimming, pair merging etc.)

This subworkflow can perform:

- Adapter removal
- Read quality trimming
- Read pair merging
- Length filtering

With fastp.

Removing adapters (if present) is recommend to reduce false-postive hits that may occur from 'dirty' or 'contaminated' reference genomes in a profiling database that contain accidentially incorporated adapter sequences. Note that some, but not all, tools support paired-end alignment (utilising information about the insert covered by the pairs). However read pair merging in some cases can be recommend to increase read length (such as in aDNA). Length filtering can speed up alignment by reducing the number of short unspecific reads that need to be aligned.

shortread_qc_skipadaptertrim.help_text:
Skip the removal of sequencing adapters. 

This often can be useful to speed up run-time of the pipeline when analysing data downloaded from public databases such as the ENA or SRA, as adapters should already be removed (however we recommend to check FastQC results to ensure this is the case).

shortread_qc_adapter1.help_text:
Specify a custom forward or R1 adapter sequence to be removed from reads. 

If not set, the fastp defaults will be used.

> Modifies fastp parameter: `--adapter_sequence`. fastp default: `AGATCGGAAGAGCACACGTCTGAACTCCAGTCA`

shortread_qc_adapter2.help_text:
Specify a custom reverse or R2 adapter sequence to be removed from reads. 

If not set, the fastp defaults will be used (adapter detection for paired-end reads).

> Modifies fastp parameter: `--adapter_sequence_r2`. fastp default: `AGATCGGAAGAGCGTCGTGTAGGGAAAGAGTGT`

shortread_qc_adapterlist.description: Specify a list of all possible adapters to trim. Overrides --shortread_qc_adapter1/2. Format: FASTA.
shortread_qc_adapterlist.help_text:
Allows to supply a file with a list of adapter (combinations) to remove from all files. 

Overrides the --shortread_qc_adapter1/--shortread_qc_adapter2 parameters . 

This consists of a standard FASTA format with a `.fasta`/`.fa`/`.fna`/`.fas` extension. The adapter sequence in this file should be at least 6bp long, otherwise it will be skipped. fastp trims the adapters present in the FASTA file one by one.

> Modifies fastp parameter: --adapter_fasta

shortread_qc_mergepairs.description: Turn on merging of read pairs for paired-end data
shortread_qc_mergepairs.help_text:
Turn on the merging of read-pairs of paired-end short read sequencing data. 

> Modifies fastp parameter(s): `-m --merged_out`

shortread_qc_includeunmerged.description: Include unmerged reads from paired-end merging in the downstream analysis
shortread_qc_includeunmerged.help_text:
Turns on the inclusion of unmerged reads in resulting FASTQ file from merging paired-end sequencing data with fastp: the unmerged read pairs are directly included in the output FASTQ file.

Excluding unmerged reads can be useful in cases where you prefer to have very short reads (e.g. aDNA), thus excluding longer-reads or possibly faulty reads where one of the pair was discarded.

> Adds `fastp` option: `--include_unmerged`

shortread_qc_minlength.description: Specify the minimum length of reads to be retained
shortread_qc_minlength.help_text:
Specifying a mimum read length filtering can speed up profiling by reducing the number of short unspecific reads that need to be match/aligned to the database.

> Modifies fastp parameter: `--length_required`

shortread_qc_dedup.description: Perform deduplication of the input reads (fastp only)
shortread_qc_dedup.help_text:
This enables the deduplication of processed reads during fastp adapter removal and/or merging. It removes identical reads that are likely artefacts from laboratory protocols (e.g. amplification), and provide no additional sequence information to the library.

Removing duplicates can increase runtime and increase accuracy of abundance calculations.

> Modifies tool parameter(s):
> fastp: ` --dedup`

preprocessing_long_read_qc_options.title: Preprocessing long-read QC options
preprocessing_long_read_qc_options.description: Options for adapter clipping, quality trimming, and length filtering

perform_longread_qc.description: Turns on the quality filtering of the long reads
perform_longread_qc.help_text: Turns on the quality filtering of the long reads with vsearch (by default, removes the reads with more than 10 expected errors or with Ns) and BBDuk (by default, removes the reads with a base of quality below 3). The defaults are optimised for full-length 16S amplicons.

preprocessing_host_removal_options.title: Preprocessing host removal options
preprocessing_host_removal_options.description: Options for pre-profiling host read removal

perform_shortread_hostremoval.help_text:
Turns on the ability to remove short-reads from the that derived from a known organism, using Bowtie2 and samtools

This subworkflow is useful to remove reads that may come from a host, or a known contamination like the human reference genome. Human DNA contamination of (microbial) reference genomes is well known, so removal of these prior profiling both reduces the risks of false positives, and in _some cases_ a faster runtime (as less reads need to be profiled).

Alternatively, you can include the reference genome within your profiling databases and can turn off this subworkflow, with the trade off of a larger taxonomic profiling database.

hostremoval_reference.description: Specify path to single reference FASTA of host(s) genome(s)
hostremoval_reference.help_text:
Specify a path to the FASTA file (optionally gzipped) of the reference genome of the organism to be removed.

If you have two or more host organisms or contaminants you wish to remove, you can concatenate the FASTAs of the different taxa into a single one to provide to the pipeline.

shortread_hostremoval_index.description: Specify path to the directory containing pre-made BowTie2 indexes of the host removal reference
shortread_hostremoval_index.help_text:
Specify the path to a _directory_ containing pre-made Bowtie2 reference index files (i.e. the directory containing `.bt1`, `.bt2` files etc.). These should sit in the same directory alongside the the reference file specified in `--hostremoval_reference`.

Specifying premade indices can speed up runtime of the host-removal step, however if not supplied the pipeline will generate the indices for you.

save_hostremoval_index.description: Save mapping index of input reference when not already supplied by user
save_hostremoval_index.help_text:
Save the output files of the in-built indexing of the host genome.

This is recommend to be turned on if you plan to use the same reference genome multiple times, as supplying the directory to `--shortread_hostremoval_index` can speed up runtime of future runs. Once generated, we recommend you place this file _outside_ of your run results directory in a central 'cache' directory you and others using your machine can access and supply to the pipeline.

save_hostremoval_bam.description: Saved mapped and unmapped reads in BAM format from host removal
save_hostremoval_bam.help_text:
Save the reads mapped to the reference genome and off-target reads in BAM format as output by the respective hostremoval alignment tool.

This can be useful if you wish to perform other analyses on the host organism (such as host-microbe interaction), however, you should consider whether the default mapping parameters of Bowtie2 are optimised to your context.

save_hostremoval_unmapped.description: Save reads from samples that went through the host-removal step
save_hostremoval_unmapped.help_text:
Save only the reads NOT mapped to the reference genome in FASTQ format (as exported from `samtools view` and `fastq`).

This can be useful if you wish to perform other analyses on the off-target reads from the host mapping, such as manual profiling or _de novo_ assembly.

pathseq_t2t_options.title: PathSeq-T2T host filtering options
pathseq_t2t_options.description: Stringent host filtering of low-biomass human samples, after PathSeq-T2T (Dohlman et al., Cell 2026 (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2026.04.015)). See docs/pathseq_t2t.md

pathseq_t2t.description: Filter the host reads with PathSeq-T2T, for low-biomass human samples
pathseq_t2t.help_text: Replaces the short-read QC and host removal with the PathSeq-T2T host filtering of Dohlman et al., Cell 2026 (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2026.04.015): alignment to GRCh38 with `bwa mem -T 0`, selection of the reads not aligned to it (and of those aligned to its viral decoy contigs), GATK PathSeqFilterSpark (quality, complexity, host k-mer and duplicate filters), and removal of the reads aligned to T2T-CHM13. Only Illumina WGS FASTQ are accepted, and `--perform_shortread_qc` and `--perform_shortread_hostremoval` must be off, as well as `--run_cayman` and `--run_gqlib`. The differences from the upstream implementation (https://github.com/abdohlman/pathseq-t2t) are listed in docs/pathseq_t2t.md.

pathseq_t2t_grch38_reference.description: FASTA of GRCh38, to build its bwa index if --pathseq_t2t_grch38_bwa_index is not given
pathseq_t2t_grch38_reference.help_text: The paper uses the GRCh38 of the NCI Genomic Data Commons, with its viral decoy contigs (GRCh38.d1.vd1): https://api.gdc.cancer.gov/data/254f697d-310d-4d7d-a27b-27fbf767a834

pathseq_t2t_grch38_bwa_index.description: Directory of the bwa index of GRCh38 (the .amb, .ann, .bwt, .pac and .sa files)

pathseq_t2t_chm13_reference.description: FASTA of T2T-CHM13, to build its bwa index if --pathseq_t2t_chm13_bwa_index is not given

pathseq_t2t_chm13_bwa_index.description: Directory of the bwa index of T2T-CHM13 (the .amb, .ann, .bwt, .pac and .sa files)

pathseq_host_dir.description: Directory of the PathSeq host files pathseq_host.bfi and pathseq_host.fa.img
pathseq_host_dir.help_text: From the GATK PathSeq resource bundle: ftp://gsapubftp-anonymous@ftp.broadinstitute.org/bundle/pathseq/pathseq_host.tar.gz

pathseq_decoys_bed.description: BED of the viral decoy contigs of GRCh38, whose reads are kept; empty to remove them as host reads

pathseq_min_clipped_read_length.description: Minimum read length after clipping in PathSeqFilterSpark (--min-clipped-read-length)

save_pathseq_t2t_bams.description: Save the BAMs of the PathSeq-T2T filtering steps

perform_runmerging.help_text:
Turns on the concatenation of sequencing runs or libraries with the same sample name.

This can be useful to ensure you get a single profile per sample, rather than one profile per run or library. Note that in some cases comparing profiles of independent _libraries_ may be useful, so this parameter may not always be suitable.

The runs of a sample are merged separately for each library strategy (`library_strategy` column, WGS or AMPLICON): a merged run is named `merged_WGS` or `merged_AMPLICON`, and a sample with a single run of a strategy keeps its run accession. All the runs of a sample and strategy must have the same instrument platform, file type and, unless the pairs are merged with `--shortread_qc_mergepairs`, endedness, otherwise the pipeline stops with an error.

save_runmerged_reads.description: Save reads from samples that went through the run-merging step
save_runmerged_reads.help_text:
Save the run- and library-concatenated reads of a given sample in FASTQ format.

> ⚠️ Only samples that went through the run-merging step of the pipeline will be stored in the resulting directory. 

If you wish to save the files that go to the classification/profiling steps for samples that _did not_ go through run merging, you must supply the appropriate upstream `--save_<preprocessing_step>` flag.

run_motus4.description: Turn on profiling with mOTUs v4. Requires database to be present CSV file passed to --databases

run_motus3.description: Turn on profiling with mOTUs v3. Requires database to be present CSV file passed to --databases

motus4_rename_reads.description: Whether to fix individual PE read names so that they are identical and do not have /1 or /2 suffixes
motus4_rename_reads.help_text: mOTUs 4 requires PE reads to have identical names. If the individual read names from the fastq @ lines have suffixes /1 and /2, mOTUs will fail. This step renames the reads throughout the file by removing the /1 or /2 suffix. Note that if PE reads are mismatched this step does not fix it, for that use `params.repair_pe_reads`

run_cayman.description: Turn on profiling with cayman. Requires database CSV file passed to --databases
run_cayman.help_text: Each cayman database is a row of the database CSV with db_path the gene catalogue fasta that the reads are aligned to with bwa mem, and annot_db_path the cayman annotation table (.csv), named by annot_db_name. The bwa index files, as created by `bwa index <fasta>` (<fasta>.amb, .ann, .bwt, .pac, .sa), must be in the same directory as the fasta. The pipeline does not build the bwa index: it must be created beforehand with `bwa index <fasta>` (see the database documentation). The fasta itself is not read by the pipeline, only used to locate the index files, but it must exist. Several annotations of the same gene catalogue can be profiled by adding a row for each with the same db_name and db_path and a different annot_db_name. The reads are aligned only once to each gene catalogue: all the cayman and gqlib rows with the same db_name and db_path share the alignment.

run_gqlib.description: Turn on gene-level profiling with gqlib. Requires database CSV file passed to --databases
run_gqlib.help_text: Each gqlib database is a row of the database CSV with db_path the gene catalogue fasta that the reads are aligned to with bwa mem, and annot_db_path the gqlib annotation database (.sqlite3), named by annot_db_name. The bwa index files, as created by `bwa index <fasta>` (<fasta>.amb, .ann, .bwt, .pac, .sa), must be in the same directory as the fasta. The pipeline does not build the bwa index: it must be created beforehand with `bwa index <fasta>` (see the database documentation). The fasta itself is not read by the pipeline, only used to locate the index files, but it must exist. Reads are counted on all genes of the catalogue, and the gene counts are summarised for each functional category of the annotation database. Several annotations of the same gene catalogue can be profiled by adding a row for each with the same db_name and db_path and a different annot_db_name. The reads are aligned only once to each gene catalogue: all the cayman and gqlib rows with the same db_name and db_path share the alignment.

save_bwa_alignments.description: Save the bwa mem alignments of the reads to the cayman and gqlib gene catalogues
save_bwa_alignments.help_text: The unsorted BAM files are saved to `--outdir` under `bwa/<db_name>/`. The alignments contain all hits of each read (`bwa mem -a`) and can be large.

run_kraken2.description: Classify the WGS reads with Kraken2, against the kraken2 databases of the database sheet
run_kraken2.help_text: The options of a database (db_params) default to `--report-minimizer-data`, with `--confidence 0.15` added with --pathseq_t2t (which does not accept db_params for Kraken2), as in PathSeq-T2T (Dohlman et al., Cell 2026, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2026.04.015), which used the PlusPF database of 2024-06-05 (https://benlangmead.github.io/aws-indexes/k2). With --pathseq_t2t, the reads left without their mate are classified too. The reports are merged into tables of reads per taxon (--run_profile_standardisation).

run_idtaxa.description: Turn on taxonomic classification of amplicon reads with IDTAXA. Requires database CSV file passed to --databases
run_idtaxa.help_text: IDTAXA (DECIPHER) classifies the AMPLICON samples (library_strategy column of the samplesheet) against a training set, the db_path of an idtaxa row of the database CSV (.RData, as distributed with DECIPHER). The pairs of paired-end reads are merged if they overlap, the others are handled as set by `--amplicon_pair_handling`. The confidence threshold is set with `--idtaxa_threshold`, the strand of the sequences (both for the short reads, top for the long reads, oriented by the primer trimming) with `ext.strand` in a custom config.

idtaxa_db_names.description: Comma-separated db_name of the idtaxa rows of the database CSV to classify against. All idtaxa rows if not set
idtaxa_db_names.help_text: The database CSV can list several IDTAXA training sets (e.g. different GTDB releases, such as R220 to match the taxonomy of mOTUs 4.0 used for the WGS samples, or SILVA), and this chooses among them by their db_name, e.g. `--idtaxa_db_names gtdb_r220` or `--idtaxa_db_names gtdb_r220,silva_r138_2`. The other idtaxa rows are ignored. A name not among the idtaxa rows of the database CSV is an error.

idtaxa_threshold.description: Minimum confidence (0-100) of the taxa assigned by IDTAXA
idtaxa_threshold.help_text: The minimum confidence (0-100) at which IdTaxa assigns a taxon: the lineage of a sequence stops at the last rank assigned above it. DECIPHER suggests 60 (very high confidence), 50 (high confidence) or 40 (moderate confidence). The default, 40, is that of vknight. Passed to IdTaxa as its `threshold`.

idtaxa_ranks.description: Comma-separated ranks to write a merged IDTAXA table for. All the ranks if not set
idtaxa_ranks.help_text: The merged IDTAXA tables have one table of the whole lineages, as assigned, and one table per rank (domain, phylum, ..., genus), with the lineages cut at that rank and the sequences not assigned down to it in the row unassigned. By default there is a table for each rank of the lineages; with a comma-separated list of ranks (as named in the training set, e.g. `genus` or `family,genus`), only for those. A rank that no lineage reaches gives a table with only the unassigned sequences.

run_profile_standardisation.description: Turn on standardisation of taxon tables across profilers
run_profile_standardisation.help_text: Turns on standardisation of output OTU tables across all tools.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The results are published to the output directory by the workflow outputs of Nextflow (the output block of main.nf). This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to save these files (`workflow.output.mode`). See [Nextflow docs](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/config/workflow) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).

skip_multiqc.description: Should the generation of the multiwc report be skipped?

skip_postprocessing_qc.description: Specify to skip sequencing quality control of the reads given to the profilers, after all the preprocessing

skip_hostremoval_qc.description: Skip the generation of alignment statistics for hostremoval
